ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
A charged particle with negligible gravity and a charge-to-mass ratio of $k$ is injected from point $P$ at coordinates $(0, a)$ with a certain velocity parallel to the $x$-axis into a circular uniform magnetic field region of radius $R$ with a magnetic induction strength of $B$ and a direction perpendicular to the plane of the paper outward. The particle exits the magnetic field at point $Q$ on the $x$-axis, with the direction of the exit velocity at an angle of $60^{\circ}$ to the positive $x$-axis.

1. Find the radius of the trajectory $r$.
2. What is the velocity $v$ of a charged particle entering a magnetic field?
3. What is the time for the particle to move from point $P$ to point $Q$?

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure has rectangular coordinate axes, with the y axis vertically upward and the x axis horizontally to the right; the circular dashed/dotted region indicates a uniform magnetic field region perpendicular to the paper outward. Point P is on the y axis, marked at the position of height a, and the incident velocity arrow v points horizontally to the right from P. Point Q is on the x axis, and the outgoing direction at Q makes 60° with the positive x axis; in the figure this direction is inclined toward the lower right. Reasoning: Take the ratio of charge amount to mass as k. In magnetic field B it undergoes uniform circular motion, the angular velocity is kB, and the trajectory radius satisfies r = v/(kB). Since B is perpendicular to the paper outward and the incident velocity at point P is to the right, positive k corresponds to the Lorentz force downward, so the trajectory bends clockwise; therefore the trajectory center C is directly below point P, PC = r, so y_C = a - r. The outgoing velocity direction at point Q makes -60° with the positive x axis, and radius CQ must be perpendicular to the velocity; for clockwise motion, the radius direction from C to Q makes 30° with the positive x axis. Therefore the vertical coordinate of point Q is y_Q = y_C + r sin30° = a - r + r/2. Also Q is on the x axis, so y_Q=0, obtaining a - r/2 = 0, namely r = 2a. Thus v = kBr = 2kBa. From P to Q, the radius direction turns from 90° to 30°, turning through central angle 60° = π/3; the angular velocity is kB, so the motion time t = (π/3)/(kB) = π/(3kB).
